jobs.prompt:
fix(cpp): make regular-expression execution limits deterministic so a slow or busy host cannot fail legitimate requests

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `claude/cpp-gateway-port` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: the delivered native C++20 gateway (`cpp/gateway/`), C++ only (do NOT install or run Bun, Node, Deno, Rust or Cargo). It will be deployed for a week of real-world testing on a small 2-core ARM64 server. Read `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (driver: `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release|asan <test>`), `cpp/gateway/docs/SECURITY-LIMITS.md`, `cpp/gateway/include/uos/rt/limits.hpp`, `cpp/gateway/src/rt/regex*.cpp` (the engine is the vendored QuickJS-ng `libregexp` under `third_party/`), and `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md`. Your branch becomes a pull request; your final message is its body (short, plain language).

THE DEFECT: regular-expression execution is bounded by WALL-CLOCK deadlines (`kRegexCompileDeadline` 10 ms, `kRegexDeadline` 250 ms, `kRegexLargeSubjectDeadline` 1,800 ms for fixed image/compaction/SSE patterns on subjects over 1 MiB, and a 1,250 ms budget for the supervisor credential-redaction pattern). On a loaded machine the same legitimate input takes longer and the limit fires: the hosted CI just failed `tests/jev_compaction_test.cpp`, case "floor-bound summary ships for a roughly 1.5-million-token input that cannot shrink further", under the sanitizer build with `uncaught exception: regular expression execution limit exceeded`, although the same commit passes that case on an idle runner. In production this means a busy or slow host can reject a legitimate large request (compaction of a long conversation, a large image payload, a long provider stream) depending on CPU contention. A limit that depends on machine speed is neither a reliable denial-of-service bound nor safe for legitimate traffic.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner, Ubuntu 26.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network. `sudo apt-get install -y clang ninja-build pkg-config ccache libboost-json-dev libboost-container-dev libssl-dev libsqlite3-dev zlib1g-dev libicu-dev libbrotli-dev libzstd-dev` gives a toolchain that builds this tree (the CI workflow shows the exact package list and how it builds the pinned SQLite: do the same). The environment has `CCACHE_DIR` set to a directory that is restored before and saved after your job; `ccache` is installed.


RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Tests use local mocks only.
- Your process can be restarted without warning and then knows only what is committed: commit after each step, keep a checklist in `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-regex-budget-20261120.md`, read it and `git log` first after a restart. No foreground command longer than about 10 minutes.
- Do not delete or weaken tests. Security must not get weaker: every pattern/subject that the limits reject today for being pathological must still be rejected, deterministically.
- Vendored sources under `third_party/` stay byte-identical: use the engine's public hooks only (it calls an interrupt/timeout check callback periodically during matching and a stack check; see how `src/rt/regex*.cpp` wires `lre_check_timeout`/`lre_check_stack_overflow` or their equivalents).

TASK
1. Replace the wall-clock execution limit with a DETERMINISTIC work budget: count the engine's periodic interrupt callbacks (each represents a fixed amount of matcher work) and stop when a budget is exceeded. The budget is a function of the inputs only: a base allowance plus an allowance proportional to subject length (linear-time patterns need work proportional to the subject), with separate documented constants for the generic case and for the fixed large-subject application patterns (image, compaction, SSE, supervisor credential redaction). Calibrate the constants by measuring callback counts (not time) for: every regex executed by the existing test suite's legitimate cases (instrument a debug counter, run the regex, image, compaction, SSE, supervisor-brief, input-normalisation tests and take the maximum per category), and the known pathological cases in the tests (catastrophic backtracking patterns). Choose budgets with headroom of about 4x over the largest legitimate count per category and verify every pathological case still exceeds its budget. Record the measured counts in the report.
2. Keep wall clock only as a generous backstop against a stuck engine, large enough that it cannot fire for work within the deterministic budget even on a host 20x slower than your runner (state the arithmetic), and make its error distinguishable in logs from the budget error. Compile-time limits: bound compilation deterministically too if the engine exposes a hook (pattern length and nesting limits already exist: keep them); otherwise keep the compile wall-clock bound but raise it to a value that cannot fire on a 20x slower host for patterns within the length limit, and say so.
3. `include/uos/rt/limits.hpp` and `docs/SECURITY-LIMITS.md`: replace the time constants with the budget constants and explain in two sentences why the limit is work-based.
4. Tests: the same legitimate large inputs must pass when the process is artificially slowed (add a test hook that injects a delay into the interrupt callback, or run the regex under an injected slow clock, so the test proves independence from speed without real sleeping where possible); pathological patterns are rejected at the same callback count regardless of speed; the existing regex, compaction, image, SSE and supervisor tests pass in release and `--config asan`, including `jev_compaction_test` run 20 times in a row under asan with 4 parallel copies running to create load.
5. Search the rest of the gateway for other WALL-CLOCK limits whose expiry rejects legitimate work depending on host speed, as opposed to protocol timeouts on network peers (which are correct as time): list each with file and constant and classify it (network timeout: fine; CPU-bound work limit: same defect). Fix the CPU-bound ones the same way if the change is small; otherwise list them as follow-ups.

DONE WHEN
No legitimate regex execution can fail because of host speed (shown by the slowed-host tests and the loaded 20x repeat), pathological inputs are still rejected deterministically, the documents match, and the report lists measured counts and the audit of other time-based work limits.
